column3: NKJV has “Priscilla,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads the shorter form “Prisca.”
NKJV has “firstfruits of Achaia,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “of Asia.”
NKJV has “labored much for us,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “for you.”
NKJV has the name “Amplias,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “Ampliatus.”
Close to the Greek; NKJV lists “Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes,” reversing the Greek order “Hermes, Patrobas, Hermas.”
NKJV has “The churches of Christ,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “All the churches of Christ.”
NKJV has “our Lord Jesus Christ,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “our Lord Christ.”
NKJV has “our Lord Jesus Christ,” following the Textus Receptus; the critical text reads “our Lord Jesus.”
This verse is absent from the critical text; NKJV includes it following the Textus Receptus (a grace benediction).
